items.title: Information leakage and equivocation for finite observations
items.statement: For finite random variables $M,Z$, information leakage is the finite mutual information $I(M;Z)$ in nats, as defined in [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]], and equivocation is the finite conditional entropy $H(M\mid Z)$, as defined in [[def-it-finite-conditional-entropy]]. For an $n$-use code with Eve's observation $Z^n$, its normalized leakage is $n^{-1}I(M;Z^n)$. When $M$ is uniform on a finite message set $\mathcal M$, its entropy is $H(M)=\ln|\mathcal M|$. Zero-probability symbols are handled by the finite entropy and KL conventions cited above.
proof_obligations: Specify the finite domains, nats convention, conditional entropy and mutual information formulas, and the blocklength normalization.

items.title: Weak secrecy does not imply strong secrecy
items.statement: Consider the noiseless finite wiretap channel with $\mathcal X=\mathcal Y=\mathcal Z=\{0,1\}$ and $W(y,z\mid x)=1$ exactly when $y=z=x$. At blocklength $n$, let $k_n=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$, let $M_n$ be uniform on $\{0,1\}^{k_n}$, and transmit $X^n=(M_n,0^{n-k_n})$. Bob and Eve both observe the transmitted word exactly. This reliable code sequence satisfies weak secrecy but not strong secrecy: its leakage is $I(M_n;Z^n)=k_n\ln2\to\infty$, whereas $n^{-1}I(M_n;Z^n)\to0$. In general, strong secrecy implies weak secrecy.
proof_obligations: Construct a uniform kₙ-bit message, transmit it followed by fixed padding, and verify zero Bob error.
Compute I(Mₙ;Zⁿ)=kₙ ln 2 exactly and check both normalizations.
Prove strong secrecy implies weak secrecy for every sequence by nonnegativity and n≥1.

items.title: A degraded binary erasure wiretap channel
items.statement: Bob observes a binary erasure channel (BEC) with input alphabet $\{0,1\}$, output alphabet $\{0,1,e\}$, and erasure probability $1/4$. Eve observes Bob's output after independently erasing each surviving bit with probability $1/3$, while an erasure remains an erasure. This is a finite degraded wiretap channel. Its strong- and weak-secrecy capacities under average or maximal error are all $\ln2/4$ nats per use. Define $h(p):=-p\ln p-(1-p)\ln(1-p)$ with $0\ln0:=0$. For Bernoulli-$p$ input the single-letter difference is $h(p)/4$, which is zero at $p=0,1$ and maximal at $p=1/2$.
proof_obligations: Verify the extra-erasure cascade gives BEC(1/2) and physical degradation.
Compute the conditional entropy and mutual information of a BEC under arbitrary Bernoulli(p) input.
Maximize h(p) including the endpoints p=0,1.
